title: U.S. House · California's 25th District
area: Imperial County and parts of Riverside and San Bernardino counties, including the Coachella Valley (Indio, Coachella, Cathedral City) and Inland Empire and Imperial County cities such as Hemet, San Jacinto, El Centro, Calexico, and Needles. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.
Incumbent Democrat Raul Ruiz advanced from California's June 2, 2026 top-two primary along with Republican Joe Males, a Hemet City Council member.

candidates.name: Raul Ruiz
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, CA-25 (since 2013, representing the 36th District 2013-2023 and the 25th District since 2023)

summary.text: Raul Ruiz is the Democratic incumbent for California's 25th Congressional District, a physician first elected to the U.S. House in 2012. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

background.text: Born in Zacatecas, Mexico, and graduated from Coachella Valley High School in 1990. Earned a bachelor's degree from UCLA in 1994, a medical degree and master's degree in public policy from Harvard University in 2001, and a master's degree in public health from Harvard in 2007.
Worked as an emergency room physician and an associate dean with the University of California, Riverside School of Medicine before entering Congress.

positions.summary: Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and cosponsored the Climate Action Now Act to keep the U.S. on track with Paris Agreement emissions goals.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz also helped bring the Inflation Reduction Act across the finish line, which makes the single largest investment ever in combatting climate change while bringing clean energy manufacturing jobs to local communities.

positions.summary: Authored legislation signed into law to strengthen and expand Medicaid coverage for children and families with mental health needs.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz has also gotten legislation signed into law to strengthen and expand Medicaid.

positions.summary: Supports increased border security funding and technology while also backing a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and farmworkers, opposing their deportation.
positions.quote: Dr. Ruiz supports securing our borders with smart, modern technology while maintaining professionalism and humanity in our immigration system.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology Subcommittee; Health Subcommittee; Environment Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Joe Males is the Republican nominee for California's 25th Congressional District. He is a Marine Corps veteran, small-business owner, and member of the Hemet City Council.

background.text: Enlisted in the Marine Corps after turning 18, attended boot camp at Camp Pendleton, and served overseas in the Philippines and Guam before being honorably discharged as a Sergeant.
Built a computer-networking services business starting in 1996, after entering the field in an entry-level position.
Elected to the Hemet City Council after his son, a fellow Marine, was killed; he has said this motivated his entry into public safety-focused local politics.

priorities.text: Describes his campaign as bringing "Leadership & Commonsense Solutions to Washington for the people of the Inland Empire and Imperial County."
On the Hemet City Council, says he has led initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean.

researchNotes: Raul Ruiz has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current issue-by-issue statements were found within this session's time budget beyond his committee role, so no positions are listed; his federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Joe Males has not completed the Candidate Connection survey either; his campaign website did not include a dedicated issues page reachable in this session, so positions are limited to general priorities language.
